title: Odd and even functions
keyIdea: A function is even when f(−x) = f(x) for every x: its graph is its own mirror image in the y-axis. It is odd when f(−x) = −f(x) for every x: a half turn about the origin leaves its graph unchanged. Most functions are neither. To test one, work out f(−x) and compare it with f(x) and with −f(x).

kid: Put −x into a function and see what comes out. If f(−x) = f(x) every time, f is even. The graph is the same on both sides of the y-axis, like a fold. x² is even, since (−3)² = 9 = 3².
If f(−x) = −f(x) every time, f is odd. Each output keeps its size but flips its sign. Turn the graph a half turn about O and it lands on itself. x³ is odd, since (−2)³ = −8.
Many functions are neither. x³ + 1 is not odd: f(1) = 2 but f(−1) = 0. One pair that fails is enough to rule a test out. But one pair that works does not prove a test passes.

For a polynomial, check the powers. Even powers and constants keep their sign. Odd powers flip. So x⁴ − 4x² is even and x³ − 4x is odd. cos x is even and sin x is odd. If f is odd and defined at 0, then f(0) = 0.
adult: This A-level topic (ages 16 to 18) asks learners to classify functions as even, with f(−x) = f(x) and symmetry in the y-axis, or odd, with f(−x) = −f(x) and rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin. The tests must hold for every x in a domain that is symmetric about 0.

The algebraic test is to simplify f(−x) and compare it with f(x) and with −f(x). For polynomials this reduces to the powers: only even powers (constants count as x⁰) gives even, only odd powers gives odd. Products follow sign rules: odd × odd is even, odd × even is odd, so x sin x is even.

Common mistakes: calling x³ + 1 odd because x³ is; thinking a constant breaks evenness; judging from one pair of values, which can only disprove a test; reading (x − 1)² as even because it is a mirror shape about another line; and forgetting that an odd function defined at 0 must pass through the origin.

In the lab, learners drag a point P and watch its partner Q at −x against a mirror ring and a half-turn ring. They turn a copy of x³ and x², sort six graphs, build an odd graph from its right half to hit two targets, and switch polynomial powers on and off. The challenge mixes classifying with using f(−a).

familyTip: Fold a sheet of squared paper down the middle and draw half a curve on one side. Press it to copy onto the other side: that is an even graph. Then try turning the sheet upside down to make an odd one.

practice.prompt: f is an odd function and f({a}) = {b}. What is f(−{a})?
practice.hint: Odd means f(−x) = −f(x): the output keeps its size but flips its sign.
practice.explain: For an odd function the output flips sign, so f(−{a}) = −f({a}) = −{b}.

practice.prompt: g is an even function and g(−{a}) = {b}. What is g({a})?
practice.hint: Even means the outputs at x and −x are equal.
practice.explain: For an even function g(x) = g(−x), so g({a}) = g(−{a}) = {b}.

practice.prompt: Which of these functions is even?
practice.hint: Look for a function with only even powers. A constant counts as x⁰.
practice.explain: x⁴, x² and the constant 5 all keep their sign when x becomes −x, so f(−x) = f(x). x³ + x is odd and x² + x is neither.

practice.prompt: What is f(−x) when f(x) = x³ − 4x?
A graph is unchanged by a half turn about the origin. What kind of function is it?
practice.hint: A half turn sends (x, y) to (−x, −y).
practice.explain: If (x, y) on the graph always gives (−x, −y) on the graph, then f(−x) = −f(x): the function is odd.

pool.prompt: Is f(x) = x³ + 1 odd, even or neither?
pool.hint: Work out f(1) and f(−1). Are they equal, opposite or neither?
pool.explain: f(1) = 2 and f(−1) = 0. These are neither equal nor opposite, so f is neither. The + 1 spoils the odd symmetry of x³.

pool.prompt: Is f(x) = x sin x odd, even or neither?
pool.hint: x is odd and sin x is odd. What is odd × odd?
pool.explain: f(−x) = (−x)sin(−x) = (−x)(−sin x) = x sin x = f(x), so f is even.

pool.prompt: Why is cos x an even function?
choices: cos(−x) = cos x, so its graph is symmetric in the y-axis
Its graph passes through the origin
pool.hint: Compare the cosine graph on each side of the y-axis.
pool.explain: The angle −x has the same x-coordinate on the unit circle as x, so cos(−x) = cos x. That is the even rule.

pool.prompt: f is odd and defined for every x. What is f(0)?
pool.explain: f(−0) = −f(0) means f(0) = −f(0), so 2f(0) = 0 and f(0) = 0. The graph must pass through the origin.

pool.prompt: Ana says f(x) = (x − 1)² is even because its graph is a symmetric U. What is wrong?
choices: Its mirror line is x = 1, not the y-axis
It is odd, because of the minus sign
pool.explain: Even means symmetric in the y-axis. (x − 1)² is symmetric about x = 1: f(−1) = 4 but f(1) = 0.

pool.prompt: Ben checks f(2) = −f(−2) for one function and says it is odd. Is that enough?
choices: No: the rule must hold for every x
pool.hint: Could another x break the rule?
pool.explain: One pair can rule a test out but cannot prove it. For example x⁴ − 4x² gives f(2) = 0 = −f(−2), yet it is even, not odd.

pool.hint: Odd needs only odd powers and no constant.
pool.explain: Every term in x⁵ − 2x³ + x is an odd power, so each flips sign and f(−x) = −f(x). The other two mix odd and even powers.

pool.prompt: f(x) = x⁶ + 2x² − 7. What does the constant −7 do to the symmetry?
pool.explain: A constant is the same at x and −x, so it keeps f(−x) = f(x). Moving the graph up or down keeps y-axis symmetry.

pool.prompt: h is odd and h(−{a}) = {b}. What is h({a})?
pool.hint: Odd means h(x) = −h(−x). Flip the sign of the output you know.
pool.explain: h({a}) = −h(−{a}) = −{b}. The input changes sign and so does the output.

pool.hint: Put x = 0 into the formula. Then ask: could an odd function have this value at 0?
pool.explain: f(0) = 0³ + {a} = {a}. That is not 0, so f cannot be odd: an odd function defined at 0 must have f(0) = 0.

visual.caption: Even, odd or neither? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a point and its partner at −x, turn graphs half a turn, sort and build odd and even graphs, and switch powers on and off.
